newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-FREE STATE STUN WAIKATO WITH FOUR TRIES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FREE STATE STUN WAIKATO WITH FOUR TRIES.

text.p: South Africa's Free State kept alive their outside hopes of making the Super 12 semifinals with a 27-13 defeat of New Zealand's Waikato on Saturday.

Free State ran in four tries to one, ensuring maximum five points from the encounter. They responded to early pressure from Waikato, who led 13-10 at halftime, and dominated the final quarter, scoring three tries.

Waikato opened the scoring with a pushover try by prop forward Michael Collins in the fifth minute. Full-back Matthew Cooper converted and also kicked penalties in the 22nd and 42nd minutes to give the visitors their halftime advantage.
In reply Free State worked a try for back row forward Johan Erasmus, who drove over the line from a tap penalty five metres out.
The third quarter was scoreless but a brilliant individual effort by Free State right wing Jan-Harm van Wyk gave notice of things to come in the 62nd minute.

Van Wyk chipped over the head of left wing Eric Rush and beat the All Black to the ball in a 40-metre race. Nine minutes later a burst by number eight Jaco Coetzee created a huge overlap for full-back Jorrie Kruger to score wide on the left.
In injury time lock forward Braam Els capped a magnificent game in the tight by driving through four Waikato tackles to dot down the fourth Free State try.
Waikato take on South Africa's Gauteng Lions in Hamilton next Saturday, while Free State have a week off to recharge their batteries.

Free State: Jorrie Kruger; Jan-Harm van Wyk, Helgard Muller (captain), Brendan Venter, Stephen Brink; M.J.Smith, Werner Swanepoel; Jaco Coetzee, Johan Erasmus, Andre Venter, Braam Els, Ryno Opperman, Willie Meyer (Dougie Heymans 48), Naka Droske, Os du Randt.

Waikato: Matthew Cooper; Glen Osborne, Frank Bunce, Walter Little, Eric Rush; Ian Foster, Mark Robinson; Errol Brain, Dean Anglesey (Deon Muir 42), Aaron Hopa, Glenn Taylor, Ian Jones (captain), Richard Loe, Greg Smith (Paul Mitchell 48), Michael Collins.
